evidence: CVE.org https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-41706 has cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); CNA title is 'Open Redirect When Using CookieRequestCache'; CWE-601; impact is an attacker-influenced REDIRECT_URI cookie redirecting an authenticated user to an attacker-controlled URL after login.

Spring first-party advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-41706/ (published 2026-06-09) requires CookieRequestCache or CookieServerRequestCache plus attacker influence over the REDIRECT_URI cookie (subdomain cookie injection, response splitting, or HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade).

Source-to-sink (WebFlux): CookieServerRequestCache.getRedirectUri Base64-decodes REDIRECT_URI and maps it through URI.create with no relative/same-origin check. RedirectServerAuthenticationSuccessHandler.onAuthenticationSuccess then passes that URI to DefaultServerRedirectStrategy.sendRedirect, which sets Location to the URI unchanged when it does not start with '/'.

Source-to-sink (Servlet sibling): CookieRequestCache.saveRequest stored UrlUtils.buildFullRequestUrl (scheme/host/port/path/query) in the same cookie; getRequest decoded it and rebuilt DefaultSavedRequest from cookie-controlled scheme/host/port/path. SavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler then sendRedirects savedRequest.getRedirectUrl().

findings: CVE-2026-41706 / GHSA-x2r2-rvhq-2mqv is a real published CWE-601: CookieRequestCache and CookieServerRequestCache treat an attacker-influenced Base64 REDIRECT_URI cookie as the post-login redirect target without a relative-path/same-origin check.

Smallest surviving public first-writer is ae532c080cbd594af7eeeee99742152225de4087, which added CookieServerRequestCache.getRedirectUri as decode-then-URI.create with no validation. Parent 38979b1b09bd4affc13a45d71e56e155140d5205 has no cookie cache.

Servlet CookieRequestCache 9708a2d63fb9a1898bae7971953f21ae8aff9340 later stored absolute URLs and reconstructed scheme/host/port from the cookie; it is a sibling expansion, not the repository-first BIC.
Direct fix is a14c9d66b15946d2040a3681b55fe29ac145c5c9, present in public tags 6.5.11 and 7.0.6 and absent from 6.5.10 and 7.0.5, matching the Spring OSS fixed versions.
BIC commit object attributes both author and committer to named human Eleftheria Stein with no AI/bot/generator marker, so the primary NOT_AI verdict stands.
